case_title: Nilesh Sharma RP Today Homes and Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd. vs. Mordhwaj Singh & Ors.
material_facts: 1. PARTY IDENTITIES: Nilesh Sharma is the Resolution Professional of Today Homes and Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd. (Corporate Debtor); Mordhwaj Singh, Vikramjit Singh, Ram Narayan Singh, and Bhim Singh are original landowners/respondents; New India City Developers Pvt. Ltd. is the developer/collaborator. 2. COMMERCIAL TRANSACTION: Landowners entered into a Development Agreement on 03.03.2007 with the developer for 35.2062 acres in Behrampur, Gurugram (45% FAR to owners, 55% to developer). After arbitral consent terms and grant of licenses, the developer assigned all rights, obligations, and FSI of 8,00,000 sq. ft. on its 10.81-acre share to the Corporate Debtor vide Agreement dated 30.07.2010 (consideration Rs. 40 Crores, later enhanced to Rs. 120 Crores). The Corporate Debtor undertook the 'Canary Greens' residential housing project thereon, selling units to over 500 homebuyers. 3. DEFAULT METRICS: Operational debt defaults led to CIRP admission, with claims involving over 500 stalled homebuyers and unpaid contractual amounts under arbitration awards; specific monetary default metric was adjudicated in Section 9 proceedings. 4. STATUTORY TIMELINES: On 30.08.2019, landowners issued a notice and executed a deed revoking the irrevocable Power of Attorney dated 19.01.2010; the Corporate Debtor filed Civil Suit No. 3694 of 2019 challenging the revocation. 5. FACTUAL EVIDENCE: Registered Development Agreement dated 03.03.2007, Arbitral Consent Award dated 05.09.2009, handover order of joint receivers dated 12.10.2010, registered Irrevocable Power of Attorney dated 19.01.2010, Assignment Agreement dated 30.07.2010, Arbitral Award dated 09.12.2017 confirming possession handover as on 12.10.2010, police complaint dated 11.08.2020 after landowners forcibly entered the site, interim order dated 24.08.2020 restoring possession to the RP on 02.09.2020, and the approved Resolution Plan by 96.93% voting share of the CoC. 6. PROCEDURAL HISTORY: Section 9 petition was admitted on 31.10.2019 initiating CIRP against the Corporate Debtor. The RP filed IA No. 3356 of 2020 for restoration of possession of 10.81 acres, while landowners filed IA No. 5001 of 2021 to exclude the land from the Resolution Plan. On 05.12.2023, NCLT New Delhi Court-III disposed of the applications, holding it lacked competency to decide disputed possession and relegating the parties to a competent Civil Court.
legal_issues: 1. Whether the Adjudicating Authority erred in holding that the Resolution Professional could not place on record evidence establishing physical possession of the 10.81-acre land parcel. 2. Whether the Adjudicating Authority has jurisdiction under the IBC to determine and protect the possession and development rights of the Corporate Debtor, or whether such issues must be relegated to a Civil Court. 3. Whether the 10.81-acre project land was required to be excluded from the Corporate Debtor's CIRP and Resolution Plan.
ratio_decidendi: 1. ABSTRACT LEGAL RULE: Development rights acquired by a Corporate Debtor constitute 'property' under the Code and form part of its assets which the Resolution Professional is duty-bound to preserve, protect, and take custody of during CIRP; disputes concerning protection and possession of such rights are within the exclusive summary jurisdiction of the NCLT and cannot be relegated to a Civil Court. 2. STATUTORY INTERPRETATION: Section 3(27) of the IBC provides an expansive and inclusive definition of 'property' covering present, future, vested, or contingent interests; this includes development rights transferred under commercial development agreements. Furthermore, Section 18(1)(f) and Section 25(2)(a) mandate the RP to take control of such asset rights, while Section 14(1)(d) bars recovery of property occupied by or in possession of the Corporate Debtor. 3. EVIDENTIARY TEST APPLIED: Documented chain of title and possession established through registered development contracts, arbitral consent awards, judicial handover records, and ongoing construction on-site outweighs bare registered revocation deeds of powers of attorney or denial of actual physical possession by third-party landowners. 4. DEFINITIVE CONCLUSION: The Corporate Debtor had subsisting development rights and established possession over the 10.81 acres on which 500 homebuyer flats were constructed; the NCLT erred in abdicating jurisdiction to a Civil Court, making the land an integral asset of the CIRP that cannot be excluded from the Resolution Plan.
operative_order: Company Appeal (AT) (Insolvency) No. 1691 of 2023 is allowed; impugned order dated 05.12.2023 passed in IA No. 3356 of 2020 is set aside; IA No. 3356 of 2020 filed by the RP is allowed as prayed; IA No. 3629 of 2020 and IA No. 5001 of 2021 filed by the landowners are rejected. Parties shall bear their own costs.
summary: The Resolution Professional of Today Homes and Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd. appealed against NCLT New Delhi's order dated 05.12.2023, which held that NCLT lacked jurisdiction to decide the possession of 10.81 acres of project land ('Canary Greens') and relegated the dispute to a Civil Court. Landowners contended that their revocation of the Power of Attorney and absolute ownership excluded the land from CIRP. Setting aside NCLT's order, NCLAT held that development rights constitute 'property' under Section 3(27) of the IBC and assets under Sections 18 and 25, which NCLT is fully competent to adjudicate and protect under the Code. NCLAT directed restoration and retention of possession with the RP, rejecting the landowners' exclusion prayer.

case_title: Mordhwaj Singh & Ors. vs. Nilesh Sharma RP Today Homes and Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd.
material_facts: 1. PARTY IDENTITIES: Appellants are landowners Mordhwaj Singh, Vikramjit Singh, Ram Narayan Singh, and Bhim Singh; Respondent is Nilesh Sharma, Resolution Professional of Today Homes and Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd. (Corporate Debtor). 2. COMMERCIAL TRANSACTION: Appellants entered into a Development Agreement on 03.03.2007 granting development rights over 35.2062 acres in Gurugram to New India City Developers Pvt. Ltd., which subsequently transferred/assigned its 55% share (including 10.81 acres of group housing) and 8,00,000 sq. ft. FSI to the Corporate Debtor vide Agreement dated 30.07.2010 (amended up to Rs. 120 Crores consideration) for constructing 'Canary Greens'. 3. DEFAULT METRICS: Default in commercial construction timelines and obligations leading to arbitral awards in 2017 and subsequent Section 9 insolvency admission of the Corporate Debtor on 31.10.2019. 4. STATUTORY TIMELINES: On 30.08.2019, landowners unilaterally revoked the Irrevocable Power of Attorney dated 19.01.2010; CIRP initiated on 31.10.2019. Landowners filed IA No. 5001 of 2021 on 20.10.2021 seeking exclusion of the land from the CIRP Resolution Plan. 5. FACTUAL EVIDENCE: Arbitral Consent Award dated 05.09.2009, joint receivers' handover order dated 12.10.2010 confirming delivery of physical possession, registered Development Agreement dated 03.03.2007, Assignment Agreement dated 30.07.2010, registered deed of revocation dated 30.08.2019, pending Civil Suit No. 3694 of 2019, and CoC approval of the Resolution Plan by 96.93% voting share. 6. PROCEDURAL HISTORY: Landowners filed IA No. 5001 of 2021 before NCLT New Delhi Court-III requesting exclusion of 10.81 acres from the Resolution Plan. The Adjudicating Authority disposed of the application on 05.12.2023 without granting relief, holding that possession disputes are to be adjudicated by a Civil Court. Landowners appealed seeking absolute exclusion.
legal_issues: 1. Whether 10.81 acres of project land owned by the Appellants must be excluded from the CIRP and Resolution Plan under Section 18(1)(f) Explanation (a) of the IBC due to third-party ownership and revocation of Power of Attorney. 2. Whether the Adjudicating Authority erred in holding that it lacked competence to determine the rights of the Corporate Debtor under the Development Agreement.
ratio_decidendi: 1. ABSTRACT LEGAL RULE: Landowners who grant exclusive and irrevocable development rights for valid consideration cannot seek exclusion of the development project land from the Corporate Debtor's CIRP on the pretext of holding underlying ownership, as development rights constitute statutory 'property' and 'assets' under the IBC. 2. STATUTORY INTERPRETATION: Explanation (a) to Section 18(1)(f) does not exclude assets in which the Corporate Debtor holds valuable, legally transferred development and economic rights; such rights fall square within Section 3(27) of the IBC and must be protected by the RP under Section 25(2)(a). 3. EVIDENTIARY TEST APPLIED: Physical transfer of possession confirmed by an uncontested arbitral award and subsisting construction undertaken for third-party homebuyers supersedes any unilateral ex-parte revocation of agency/PoA executed shortly before the insolvency commencement date. 4. DEFINITIVE CONCLUSION: The Corporate Debtor had valid and subsisting development rights over 10.81 acres forming part of the developer's share; the landowners were not entitled to exclude this parcel from the CIRP or the CoC-approved Resolution Plan.
operative_order: Company Appeal (AT) (Insolvency) No. 331 of 2024 is dismissed; IA No. 5001 of 2021 filed by the Appellants before the Adjudicating Authority is dismissed. The parties shall bear their own costs.
summary: Landowners appealed against the order dated 05.12.2023 passed by NCLT New Delhi Court-III, contending that 10.81 acres of land in Behrampur, Gurugram should be completely excluded from the CIRP and Resolution Plan of Today Homes and Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd. on grounds of ownership and pre-CIRP revocation of the Power of Attorney. Dismissing the appeal, NCLAT held that the Corporate Debtor held valid, assignable development rights which constitute 'property' under Section 3(27) and 'assets' under Sections 18 and 25 of the IBC. Consequently, third-party landowners cannot pull the project land out of the CIRP, and their application for exclusion was rightfully dismissed.

case_title: Nilesh Sharma RP Today Homes and Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd. vs. Atul Kumar & Ors.
material_facts: 1. PARTY IDENTITIES: Nilesh Sharma, RP of Today Homes and Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd. (Corporate Debtor); Atul Kumar & Ors. (Respondents 1 to 3, landowners); Realtech Realtors Pvt. Ltd. (Respondent 4); Jai Mata Realtors Pvt. Ltd. (Respondent 5). 2. COMMERCIAL TRANSACTION: Landowners (Respondents 1-3) owned 33 acres in Behrampur, Gurugram. Under a Joint Collaboration Agreement dated 06.08.2010, the land was divided into Holding A (11.794 acres) allocated to Respondent 5, and Holding B (11.794 acres) to Respondents 1-4. On 06.08.2010, Respondent 5 transferred and assigned all FSI and development rights over Holding A to the Corporate Debtor for Rs. 110 Crores (Rs. 105 Crores paid immediately), supported by a General Power of Attorney from Respondents 1-3. The Corporate Debtor constructed 'Callidora' and 'Royal Elegancia' comprising 8 towers and over 650 flats. 3. DEFAULT METRICS: Statutory default under CIRP proceedings initiated against the Corporate Debtor; dispute over surrender and peaceful possession of 2.14 acres within Holding A. 4. STATUTORY TIMELINES: Joint Collaboration Agreement dated 06.08.2010; supplementary agreement dated 06.11.2015; CIRP admission on 31.10.2019; CoC approval of Resolution Plan on 16.08.2021 with 96.93% voting share. 5. FACTUAL EVIDENCE: Joint Collaboration Agreement dated 06.08.2010, Assignment Agreement dated 06.08.2010 with payment proofs of Rs. 105 Crores, DTCP License dated 06.01.2011, supplementary agreement dated 06.11.2015, and on-site construction of 8 towers housing 650 flats. 6. PROCEDURAL HISTORY: The RP filed IA No. 4876 of 2020 seeking directions against Respondents 1-3 to hand over peaceful, vacant possession of 2.14 acres. On 22.12.2023, NCLT New Delhi Court-III disposed of the IA relying on its earlier order dated 05.12.2023, holding that disputed possession issues can only be decided by a Competent Civil Court.
legal_issues: 1. Whether the Adjudicating Authority erred in refusing to adjudicate the RP's application for possession of 2.14 acres of project land and relegating the issue to a Civil Court. 2. Whether development rights over the collaboration land constitute property of the Corporate Debtor protected under the IBC.
ratio_decidendi: 1. ABSTRACT LEGAL RULE: Development rights acquired for valuable consideration by a Corporate Debtor constitute statutory property under Section 3(27) of the IBC, and the Adjudicating Authority has exclusive jurisdiction to protect and enforce the Resolution Professional's custody and possession of such property without delegating adjudication to ordinary civil forums. 2. STATUTORY INTERPRETATION: Section 3(27) read with Sections 18, 25(2)(a), and 60(5) gives the NCLT full authority to issue restorative and protective directions for property over which the Corporate Debtor has acquired vested development interests and where housing projects have been constructed for allottees. 3. EVIDENTIARY TEST APPLIED: Substantial payment of consideration (Rs. 105 Crores out of Rs. 110 Crores), registered collaboration agreements, and the physical erection of multi-tower housing projects establish an indefeasible property interest warranting protective summary relief against landholders attempting dispossession. 4. DEFINITIVE CONCLUSION: The NCLT's refusal to adjudicate possession of the 2.14-acre parcel based on its set-aside order dated 05.12.2023 was unsustainable, requiring the application of the RP to be allowed.
operative_order: Company Appeal (AT) (Insolvency) No. 336 of 2024 is allowed; the impugned order dated 22.12.2023 passed by the Adjudicating Authority in IA No. 4876 of 2020 is set aside; IA No. 4876 of 2020 is allowed as prayed. Parties shall bear their own costs.
summary: The Resolution Professional of Today Homes and Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd. appealed the order dated 22.12.2023 passed by NCLT New Delhi in IA No. 4876 of 2020, where NCLT refused to direct landowners to hand over possession of 2.14 acres of project land, holding that possession disputes require a Civil Court trial. Setting aside the order, NCLAT held that the Corporate Debtor acquired valid development rights over the land for Rs. 110 Crores and built over 650 flats across 8 towers. Such development rights are 'property' under Section 3(27) of the IBC, and the NCLT has full jurisdiction to protect and restore possession to the RP. The appeal and IA were allowed.

case_title: Nilesh Sharma RP Today Homes & Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd. vs. Atul Kumar & Ors.
material_facts: 1. PARTY IDENTITIES: Appellant is Nilesh Sharma, RP of Today Homes & Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd.; Respondents 1-3 are landowners (Atul Kumar & Ors.), Respondent 4 is Realtech Realtors Pvt. Ltd., and Respondent 5 is Jai Mata Realtors Pvt. Ltd. 2. COMMERCIAL TRANSACTION: Joint Collaboration Agreement dated 06.08.2010 and assignment of FSI rights by Jai Mata Realtors Pvt. Ltd. to the Corporate Debtor for Rs. 110 Crores (Rs. 105 Crores paid) to construct the 'Callidora' and 'Royal Elegancia' housing projects. 3. DEFAULT METRICS: Default in developer commitments during real estate project execution leading to CIRP under the IBC. 4. STATUTORY TIMELINES: CIRP commenced on 31.10.2019; CoC approved the composite Resolution Plan for the housing projects with 96.93% voting share on 16.08.2021; landowners filed IA No. 987 of 2021 on 20.02.2021. 5. FACTUAL EVIDENCE: Joint Collaboration Agreement dated 06.08.2010, General Power of Attorney dated 06.08.2010, DTCP license dated 06.01.2011, supplementary agreement dated 06.11.2015, and the admissions in the prayer of IA No. 987 of 2021 showing that landowners were not in physical possession of 9.675 acres. 6. PROCEDURAL HISTORY: Landowners filed IA No. 987 of 2021 under Section 60(5) seeking delivery of vacant possession of 9.675 acres and exclusion of said land from Corporate Debtor's assets. On 22.12.2023, NCLT New Delhi Court-III disposed of the IA citing lack of jurisdiction and directing the parties to Civil Court. The RP appealed the order.
legal_issues: 1. Whether the Adjudicating Authority erred in disposing of IA No. 987 of 2021 by delegating the determination of possession and asset inclusion of 9.675 acres to a Civil Court. 2. Whether landowners are entitled to seek exclusion of project land from the Corporate Debtor's CIRP where development rights are vested in the Corporate Debtor.
ratio_decidendi: 1. ABSTRACT LEGAL RULE: An Adjudicating Authority cannot avoid determining whether an immovable asset is part of the Corporate Debtor's insolvency estate; when a party seeks exclusion of land subject to vested development rights included in an approved Resolution Plan, the NCLT must adjudicate and reject such exclusion under the IBC rather than relegating the matter to a Civil Court. 2. STATUTORY INTERPRETATION: Section 60(5) of the IBC vests the NCLT with plenary jurisdiction to decide questions of priorities, assets, or law arising out of or in relation to the insolvency resolution process of the Corporate Debtor, precluding civil court jurisdiction. 3. EVIDENTIARY TEST APPLIED: An application by landowners seeking delivery of possession operates as a clear admission that they lack actual possession; where the Corporate Debtor has constructed substantial multi-unit towers pursuant to paid development agreements, the land forms part of the resolution assets. 4. DEFINITIVE CONCLUSION: The Corporate Debtor successfully established that development rights in the 9.675 acres formed part of the resolution assets; the NCLT's order relegating the controversy to a Civil Court was erroneous, and the landowners' exclusion prayer was liable to be rejected outright.
operative_order: Company Appeal (AT) (Insolvency) No. 337 of 2024 is allowed; the order dated 22.12.2023 passed in IA No. 987/2021 is set aside; IA No. 987/2021 filed by Respondents No. 1 to 3 is rejected. Parties shall bear their own costs.
summary: The Resolution Professional of Today Homes & Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd. appealed against NCLT New Delhi's order dated 22.12.2023 in IA No. 987 of 2021, wherein the tribunal disposed of the landowners' application for possession and exclusion of 9.675 acres by holding that the issue must be decided by a Civil Court. NCLAT held that the NCLT has exclusive jurisdiction under Section 60(5) of the IBC to decide the inclusion of assets and development rights in CIRP. Since the Corporate Debtor had acquired valid development rights and constructed residential projects included in an approved Resolution Plan, NCLAT set aside the impugned order, allowed the appeal, and dismissed the landowners' application.
